correctness.rationale: In a finite local ring Z(R)=m, so adjacency is determined by opposite residue classes. Characteristic 2 gives q isolated K_m components; odd characteristic gives K_m plus (q-1)/2 disjoint K_(m,m). Nonfield implies m/m^2 is a nonzero R/m-vector space, so m>=q. Component automorphisms give both wreath decompositions; bases must fix m-1 vertices in each clique or part, yielding q(m-1). A distinguishing coloring must be injective within all twin classes: q disjoint cliques require distinct m-subsets; a bipartite K_(m,m) requires unequal injective m-color subsets on its two sides. m colors fail, while m+1 suffice because q<=m, and C(m+1,2)>=(q-1)/2. Independent graphs Z/4, Z/8, Z/9, Z/16, Z/25 gave exact component sizes and Det/D (2,3),(6,5),(6,4),(14,9),(20,6), respectively. These finite checks are not the proof.
residual_risks: Finite computations are only corroboration; general statement rests on analytic proof and stated hypotheses.

value.rationale: Determining and distinguishing numbers are standard natural graph invariants measuring vertex-fixing and coloring rigidity; finite local total graphs are a canonical graph-of-ring family. The complete infinite-family formulas and equality of the ostensibly different parity regimes provide a usable classification, not merely a few computations. The ring-theoretic m>=q eliminates otherwise nontrivial component-pattern thresholds. The derivation is elementary and may become redundant if a single published general disjoint-component theorem subsumes all parts; this is recorded.
